title: Quantifying gender bias towards politicians in cross-lingual language models

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting language models to generate adjectives and verbs adjacent to politician names, then quantifying word choice and sentiment differences across male, female, and non-binary politicians using Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) and a latent-variable model.
Comparing the sentiment of words generated for politicians whose country of origin uses the target language as an official language versus politicians from other countries.
Evaluating the mean negative sentiment of words associated with the 10,000 most frequently mentioned politicians on Wikipedia compared to the broader dataset.
Comparing the sentiment of words generated for politicians born before 1946 (the Baby Boom) versus those born after 1946 to control for temporal changes in descriptions.
